summary: The selected arrow-trap path has three gaps. preflight_dotrap refuses ARROW_TRAP; once admitted, the arrow-hit exercise callback omits encumber_msg; and the later #sit branch still records note_unported for trap.c:dotrap although sit.c:dosit calls dotrap(trap, VIASITTING). The task will admit source-supported arrow cases, pass the encumbrance callback through the hit path, and wire the existing dotrap implementation into the sitting caller.

source.branch: A hero enters an unseen ARROW_TRAP on ordinary floor, causing hack.c movement preflight and then trap.c:dotrap to dispatch trapeffect_arrow_trap; the trap hits the hero and reaches thitu’s Strength-exercise tail. After that trap becomes seen, the hero uses #sit without moving, causing sit.c:dosit to call dotrap(trap, VIASITTING) and exercise the source seen-trap escape check.
callers: hack.c:domove_core and hack.c:spoteffects call the hero movement admission and trap-arrival path; trap.c:dotrap dispatches ARROW_TRAP through trapeffect_selector to trapeffect_arrow_trap.
mthrowu.c:thitu is called by trap.c:trapeffect_arrow_trap after missile damage; its nonlethal hit path calls attrib.c:exercise(A_STR, FALSE), whose after-play wrapper can call pickup.c:encumber_msg.
sit.c:dosit calls trap.c:dotrap(trap, VIASITTING) for a trap under the hero; the current recording reaches this with the previously triggered, now-seen arrow trap.
dependencies: hack.c:requireSimpleHeroDestination corresponds to js/hack.js:requireSimpleHeroDestination and calls preflight_dotrap before the hero position changes.
trap.c:dotrap common gates and selector dispatch are already implemented by js/trap_effects.js:dotrap and trapeffect_selector.
trap.c:trapeffect_arrow_trap is implemented by js/trap_effects.js:trapeffect_arrow_trap; the hit path delegates to mthrowu.c:thitu, which calls attrib.c:exercise(A_STR, FALSE) after nonlethal damage.

js/attrib.js:exerciseAttribute requires an encumberMessage callback for Strength exercise after moves begin; the adjacent JS dart-trap arm already supplies pickup.c:encumber_msg, but the arrow-trap arm does not.

C sit.c:dosit is fully mirrored by js/sit.js:dosit except its no-utrap trap branch, which records note_unported instead of calling dotrap. C discards dotrap’s return value, so the JS caller must await its effects and ignore the return.
sit.c:dosit’s branch corresponds to js/sit.js:dosit and uses the shared trap.c:dotrap path for the trap under the hero.

The later #sit action is source-valid: sit.c:dosit (400-565) calls dotrap(trap, VIASITTING) after its sitting message when the hero has no u.utrap value and t_at() returns a trap. JavaScript js/sit.js:dosit currently records note_unported('trap.c dotrap') at line 898 instead of invoking the already-ported JS dotrap; this omits the source seen-trap rn2(5) escape check and effect. The selected recording diverges at this #sit step after all 22 screens are emitted.

Upstream trap.c:dotrap (2996-3060) admits the ordinary seen-arrow escape check and then dispatches through trap.c:trapeffect_selector to trapeffect_arrow_trap (1190-1248). The existing JS arrow effect needs to pass pickup.c:encumber_msg through attrib.c:exercise for mthrowu.c:thitu’s post-damage Strength exercise, and preflight_dotrap must admit arrow traps in its type, seen-trap, and mounted-steed gates because those C branches are implemented.

The selected scope is a source-traced divergence fix in js/trap_effects.js:preflight_dotrap and trapeffect_arrow_trap, plus the missing C caller handoff in js/sit.js:dosit. The production routes are hack.c:domove_core/spoteffects and sit.c:dosit; no C recorder, game source, recipe, or recording changes are needed.
